recent_posts.title: Release Notes for Safari Technology Preview 242
recent_posts.summary: Safari Technology Preview 242 is now available for macOS Tahoe and macOS Sequoia. Key additions include CSS attr() function from CSS Values Level 5, oblique-only value for font-synthesis-style, closedby attribute on dialog elements, SVG lang/xml:lang attribute support, getAllRecords() and IDBGetAllOptions in IndexedDB, RTCRtpReceiver.jitterBufferTarget, and secure cookies on loopback hosts. Numerous bug fixes span CSS layout (anchor positioning, sticky elements, flexbox regressions), JavaScript engine correctness, HTML parser edge cases, SVG animations, scrolling behavior, WebRTC encoding, and Web API correctness including URL parsing and event listener flag preservation.

recent_posts.title: Name-only @container queries: A solution to the naming wars
recent_posts.summary: Name-only @container queries are a new CSS feature shipping in Safari 26.4 that lets developers scope styles to named containers without requiring a size condition. Unlike traditional container queries that need a min-width or similar size constraint, name-only queries use just a container name as a filter. This solves the long-standing CSS naming problem — avoiding BEM verbosity, nesting-induced specificity wars, and the need for CSS modules — by letting styles be scoped to a named container without adding specificity. Developers register containers with container-name and container-type, then wrap component styles in matching @container blocks.

recent_posts.title: Release Notes for Safari Technology Preview 241
recent_posts.summary: Safari Technology Preview 241 brings a range of new features and bug fixes across CSS, HTML, JavaScript, SVG, WebRTC, and more. New CSS features include support for the `stretch` keyword in box sizing and stable CSS scroll anchoring. HTML gains support for the `auto` keyword in the `sizes` attribute on `` elements. The Cookie Store API now supports setting `maxAge`. WebRTC adds support for the `RTCRtpCodec` dictionary. Dozens of rendering, accessibility, media, and layout bugs are resolved, including performance fixes for `ResizeObserver` and `IntersectionObserver`, SVG animation issues, and multiple CSS unit and layout regressions.

recent_posts.title: Introducing the JetStream 3 Benchmark Suite
recent_posts.summary: JetStream 3.0 is a new cross-browser benchmark suite developed collaboratively by Apple, Google, and Mozilla. It overhauls how WebAssembly and JavaScript performance is measured by replacing isolated startup/runtime phases with full lifecycle scoring (first iteration, worst case, average case), and shifting from microbenchmarks to larger real-world workloads. The WebKit team used JetStream 3 as a driver for major JavaScriptCore improvements: WasmGC allocation inlining (eliminating two-allocation patterns for ~40% gains), GC type reference counting overhaul, Cohen's type display algorithm for fast type checks, a new greedy register allocator with B+ tree interval tracking (~2x faster for large functions), polymorphic indirect call inlining, BigInt arithmetic improvements (Comba multiplication, DIV2BY1 division), and a full rewrite of the microtask queue and Promise combinators from JS builtins to C++. These changes collectively delivered roughly a 10% performance improvement from Safari 26.0 to 26.4.

recent_posts.title: Release Notes for Safari Technology Preview 240
recent_posts.summary: Safari Technology Preview 240 is now available for macOS Tahoe and macOS Sequoia. This release adds support for the `revert-rule` CSS keyword, subpixel inline layout for more precise text positioning, and expanded DOM element/attribute name character support per the WHATWG spec. Web Inspector gains contrast information in the Color Picker. The release also includes numerous bug fixes across CSS (scrollbars, hanging-punctuation), media playback (WebM, VP8, VP9, Opus, FairPlay), rendering (table layout, aspect ratio, MathML), SVG (event handling, filter rendering, animation events), scrolling (scroll snap, Navigation API hit testing), and Web Extensions (manifest.json trailing comma parsing).

recent_posts.title: WebKit Features for Safari 26.4
recent_posts.summary: Safari 26.4 ships 44 new features and 191 bug fixes. Highlights include CSS Grid Lanes (masonry-style layouts via `display: grid-lanes`), WebTransport for low-latency bidirectional communication over HTTP/3/QUIC, and the Keyboard Lock API for fullscreen web apps. Other additions: name-only container queries, threaded scroll-driven animations, ReadableByteStream with BYOB support, ReadableStream async iteration, math typography improvements, CSS Zoom fixes, WebAuthn PRF extension, and significant SVG and table layout bug fixes. The release also completes blocks-in-inline layout rewrite and begins a new CSS Grid layout engine.

recent_posts.title: Release Notes for Safari Technology Preview 239
recent_posts.summary: Safari Technology Preview 239 is now available for macOS Tahoe and macOS Sequoia. This release brings one CSS new feature (`:open` pseudo-class for `<input>` elements) and a Web Inspector enhancement adding color contrast info to the Color Picker. Bug fixes span accessibility (VoiceOver issues with aria-owned rows, splitter elements, aria-labelledby geometry), CSS layout (collapsed borders, subgrid sizing, baseline calculation, percentage heights in intrinsic-sized containers), editing (execCommand FormatBlock, text-indent flickering), forms (readonly date input bypass), MathML rendering, media (VideoFrame color range, PDF dark mode), scrolling (scroll anchoring causing blank pages or negative offsets), Web API (change/dragend events), Web Inspector (Network panel, multi-node Copy HTML), WebAssembly streaming compilation, and WebRTC (RTCPeerConnection.addIceCandidate rejection).

recent_posts.title: Release Notes for Safari Technology Preview 238
recent_posts.summary: Safari Technology Preview 238 brings several new features and bug fixes to WebKit. Key additions include threaded time-based animation resolution for improved performance, support for the CSS :open pseudo-class, customizable <select> elements via appearance: base-select, scroll anchoring to prevent viewport jumps, ReadableStream.from() and postMessage() transfer support, and WebAssembly JavaScript Promise Integration (JSPI). Security fixes address an IDN homograph phishing vulnerability. Multiple SVG, WebRTC, rendering, and Web Inspector issues are also resolved.

recent_posts.title: Release Notes for Safari Technology Preview 237
recent_posts.summary: Safari Technology Preview 237 is now available for macOS Tahoe and Sequoia, bringing numerous fixes and new features. Key additions include the `:heading` pseudo-class selector, async iteration over ReadableStream objects, Service Worker static routing Resource Timing API, and WebRTC targetLatency attribute support. The release addresses multiple accessibility issues with aria-labelledby and VoiceOver, fixes CSS @scope rules for input elements, improves SVG gradient color interpolation, and resolves various rendering bugs in tables. Web Inspector now shows individual requests in redirect chains, and Web Extensions gain runtime.getDocumentId() support.

recent_posts.title: Announcing Interop 2026
recent_posts.summary: Interop 2026 launches with collaboration between major browser vendors (Apple, Google, Microsoft, Mozilla, and Igalia) to improve cross-browser compatibility. The initiative includes 20 focus areas—15 new and 5 carryovers—covering features like anchor positioning, advanced attr(), container style queries, scroll-driven animations, view transitions, WebTransport, and JSPI for WebAssembly. Safari has already shipped many included features like contrast-color(), media pseudo-classes, and scoped custom element registries. The project uses Web Platform Tests to measure interoperability and ensure features align with web standards, making web development more consistent and reliable across browsers.
